questions.q:
In the Server Script below, why does the query use `request.requested_for` instead of a field directly on `sc_req_item`?

```javascript
gr.addQuery('request.requested_for', gs.getUserID());
```
options: gs.getUserID() only works when dot-walking a reference field
This syntax deletes any request not belonging to the current user
It's a dot-walk through the parent Request record, because `sc_req_item` doesn't store the requester directly — that field lives on `sc_request`
requested_for is a field directly on sc_req_item and the dot-walk is unnecessary
questions.explain: sc_req_item's requester lives on its parent sc_request record, reached by dot-walking through the request reference field.

questions.q: Why does the Server Script compute `state_class` itself, mapping the raw numeric `state` value to a string like `state-wip`, rather than sending the raw number to the HTML Template?
options: Raw numeric values can never be sent from a Server Script to a Client Controller
state_class is required by GlideRecord before a query can run
So the CSS class mapping logic lives in one place server-side, and the HTML Template and CSS never have to branch on numeric state values
It has no real benefit — either approach works identically
questions.explain: Keeping the state-to-class mapping in the Server Script means the HTML/CSS just reads a class name, with no duplicated branching logic on the client.

questions.q:
In this HTML Template fragment, what does `{{item.state_class}}` inside the `class` attribute accomplish?

```html
<div class="request-card {{item.state_class}}"
     ng-repeat="item in c.data.items">
```
options: It only works if state_class is a number, not a string
It deletes the request-card class if state_class is empty
It has no effect because class attributes can't contain AngularJS interpolation
It interpolates the server-computed class name directly into the rendered element's class attribute, so the matching CSS border-color rule applies automatically
questions.explain: AngularJS interpolation inside an attribute works the same as in text content — it renders the value, here producing e.g. "request-card state-wip".

options: #f0a500 (amber), matching state-wip regardless of the actual class
No color, because CSS can't select on a dynamically interpolated class
#2ecc71 (green), because the `.request-card.state-complete` selector overrides the default gray border
#ccc (gray), because state-specific rules never override the base rule
questions.explain: A more specific compound selector (.request-card.state-complete) overrides the base .request-card border-left-color for cards carrying that class.

questions.q: What does `c.viewDetails`, wired to the template's `ng-click`, actually do in the Client Controller?
options: Deletes the Requested Item from the database
Changes the item's state directly without any server-side script running
Re-runs the Server Script's GlideRecord query from the client
Calls `spNavigator.openPage` with the Requested Item's `sys_id` and table name, opening that specific item's detail page in the portal
questions.explain: c.viewDetails hands spNavigator the item's identity so it navigates to that item's own detail page — it performs no deletion or server-side state change itself.
